title: Differential effects of stress on [¹¹C]raclopride and [¹¹C]MNPA binding to striatal D₂/D₃ dopamine receptors: a PET study in conscious monkeys.
abstract: It has been reported that stress and facilitation of dopamine neuronal system are closely related. In the present study, the effects of stress on the binding of antagonist-based [¹¹C]raclopride and agonist-based (R)-2-CH3O-N-n- propylnorapomorphine ([¹¹C]MNPA) to D₂/D₃ receptors were evaluated in the striatum of conscious monkey brain. The stress state assessed from plasma cortisol level was negatively correlated with [¹¹C]raclopride binding as expected. It was noteworthy that [¹¹C]MNPA binding exhibited a positive correlation with stress state; thus, the animals with higher cortisol levels showed higher binding to D₂/D₃ receptors.
